reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and the rendered redline correctly contains no edits and no counterparty comment — consistent with an internal evidence finding.

The cited paragraphs support the conclusion: §11.3/p0132 is an abuse/AUP investigation right tied to the Subsection 11.2(b) content warranties, not a usage-, metering- or licence-compliance audit of Customer's books or systems; p0052 shows IBM meters and invoices its own Charges with no verification right against Customer.

Because an audit right against Customer is inherently adverse to us, its absence is more favourable than the playbook preferred position, so classifying this as compliant (rather than a missing-protection deviation requiring a redline) is directionally correct.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is an expected artefact where no audit clause exists and does not evidence a defect; grafting frequency/notice/5% underpayment cost-shift and no-systems-access terms onto the abuse-investigation clause would conflict with p0137's emergency/legal carve-out and p0138 and would be an inapt, directionally wrong edit.
Rationale is accurate and appropriately flags that the AUDIT parameters should be applied if a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification.
